chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah, from more than one, from Aban, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman when she enters the state of Ihram: does she wear trousers? He said, 'Yes, for what she intends by that is covering (al-sutrah).'

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And if it is the time of the obligatory prayer and there is ample time, he should perform the voluntary prayers of Ihram first, which are six rak'at, and two of them suffice for him. Then he prays the obligatory prayer and enters Ihram after it; this is superior. And if it is not the time of the obligatory prayer, he prays six rak'at.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ihram (the state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.سُرَّة: Covering/modesty (specifically referring to the purpose of wearing trousers)

ai.seo_question: Can a woman wear trousers while in the state of Ihram during Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the permissibility of women wearing trousers during Ihram, emphasizing that the primary condition is modesty (sutrah) rather than the specific garment type, a ruling derived from the flexibility of the Prophet's tradition. Al-Sheikh’s commentary adds a layer of ritual preference (istihbab), prescribing six voluntary rak'ahs before the obligatory prayer to formally enter the state of Ihram, thereby linking the physical act of dressing with spiritual preparation. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on both the literal permissibility of clothing and the recommended spiritual etiquette preceding the Hajj rites.
